relations.subject: xdcr:half-secure-replication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (configuredVia) - the security level is a property of the reference, propagating to every replication built on it
relations.evidence: Note that replication-security is established _per reference_: this means that the security level assigned to the reference (which specifies a remote cluster) is automatically assigned to all replications based on that reference.

relations.subject: xdcr:half-secure-replication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (cascadesTo) - editing the reference's security level propagates the change to existing and future replications built on it, without deleting anything
relations.evidence: From this point, any existing replication based on the edited reference is continued in half-secure form. All new replications based on the edited reference will be started in half-secure form.

relations.subject: xdcr:half-secure-replication
relations.evidence: The `secureType` field indicates that the new reference is `half` secure.

notable_absence.finding: No role named on this page either, consistent with the rest of this batch's security pages.

cross_component_finding: SECURITY IS A PER-REFERENCE PROPERTY, NOT A PER-REPLICATION ONE - a structural fact stated explicitly here ('replication-security is established _per reference_') that has no equivalent statement anywhere in round 20's reference tree or in Capella's own XDCR pages, both of which discuss security/certificates as if configuring a single connection rather than a reusable, propagating setting. This is the sharpest example in this batch of a fact that only a full creation-and-editing procedure page - as against a settings reference page - has occasion to state.
